summary: Intermittent p99 latency / 504s for repeat-chat prompts due to per-shard KV TTL desync and cache refill storms
description:
Issue summary:

Customers observed intermittent high p99 token latency and occasional 504 / streaming timeouts when sending repeated chat prompts that reuse a short prefix. The problem started at ~2026-03-10T09:20Z for LexiChat (dedicated pool in us-east) and correlated with spikes in backend KV fetch volume and backend RPC retry errors.

Impact:
- LexiChat: multiple users reported stalled streaming responses and 504s during repeat prompts; visible in their app as long delays between the first and subsequent tokens (p99 > 5s).
- Other dedicated customers in us-east experienced elevated p99s but fewer 504s.

Environment:
- prod/us-east dedicated serving pool (shared backend kv-store)
- affected model: redwood-chat-13b for LexiChat routes

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Create a chat session and send an initial prompt to warm a prefix (e.g., "Summarize the following chat ...").
2) Send 12–20 short follow-up prompts that reuse the same prefix/context within ~2 minutes.
3) Observe streaming token arrival: first prompt completes quickly; subsequent prompts sometimes stall for multiple seconds or return 504 after timeout.

Observed logs / telemetry:
- Serving runtime traces show a burst of KV prefix read RPCs per request when stall occurs (miss rate for prefix cache jumps from ~2% baseline to ~45% during incidents).
- kv-store TCP errors (ECONNRESET) and elevated RPC retry counters in the same window.
- Streaming sessions show prolonged backpressure inside the serving worker while waiting on KV fetch completion; worker-level queue length climbs and triggers request-level timeouts.
- No immediate correlation to model GPU exhaustion or scheduler throttling.

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: prefix cache eviction (thrashing) causing cold KV reads.
- Deeper trace: per-shard TTL values for prefix entries were inconsistent after a config push on 2026-03-09 that updated TTL algorithm thresholds. Some shards had shorter effective TTLs due to an off-by-one unit conversion between config bundles and runtime readers.
- Resulting behavior: when a shard's TTL expired slightly earlier, many simultaneous requests for the same hot prefix caused a cache refill stampede. The refill path performs a small but blocking CP-heavy KV aggregation call that can take ~30–300ms; when many such calls occur concurrently it exacerbates latencies and increases the probability of RPC retries to the kv-store, leading to backpressure and timeouts in the streaming pipeline.
- The cache-warmer background job that normally smooths refills had been disabled in the affected pool (flagged as part of an earlier experiment) which magnified the effect.
- Repro on staging: reproduced by artificially desyncing TTL between two replica groups and disabling warmers; observed same p99 spike and streaming stalls.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Re-enabled cache-warmer flag on LexiChat's dedicated pool (rollout completed 2026-03-10T12:00Z).
- Increased per-prefix soft TTL floor on the affected shards to prevent micro-evictions (applied as emergency config 2026-03-10T12:30Z).
- Added a per-prefix in-flight request coalescing gate in front of the KV refill path to ensure only one refill RPC per prefix per short window (hotfix PR referenced below).

Customer-facing workaround provided:
- Advised LexiChat to add a lightweight client-side micro-batching of repeat prompts (delay 50–100ms) to avoid synchronously hammering the same prefix while we roll fixes.

Longer-term fixes and follow-ups:
- Root cause fix merged to ensure consistent TTL encoding across config bundles and runtime readers (PR github.com/redwood/re-runtime/pull/487).
- Permanent gating + smarter jitter for cache-warmers to avoid coordinated refills (PR github.com/redwood/re-runtime/pull/492).
- Improve observability: add a serving-runtime metric for per-prefix refill concurrency and a sentinel alert for refill storms.
- Runbook update: add steps to quickly re-enable warmers and apply TTL-floor if refill storm detected.

Resolution notes (in-flight):
- Immediate mitigations reduced incidents for LexiChat; we observed the prefix cache miss rate fall back to baseline within ~45 minutes of the emergency changes.
- SRE and runtime teams are scheduling the TTL encoding fix and the coalescing logic for early-week production deploy (target: 2026-03-14).

References/links:
- Incident Slack thread: #incidents • thread:IC-2026-03-10-kv-ttl-desync
- Staging replication steps: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/KV+TTL+Desync+Repro
- Related tickets: SUP-23918 (prefetch race), SUP-22109 (kv shard collisions)
comments: Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-10: Initial report from LexiChat attached; customer reports repeated short prompts stall. Opened incident and assigned to SRE.
Oliver Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Identified per-shard TTL inconsistency after config push. Re-enabled cache-warmer and applied TTL floor. Monitoring for regression.
Aria Gomez (Runtime Eng) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed desync bug reproduced in staging; preparing PR for consistent encoding. Added coalescing gate prototype (benchmarks look promising).
LexiChat Support Contact (customer) - 2026-03-11: Noted improvement after mitigation; still occasionally sees single-user stalls during peak traffic. Asked for ETA on permanent fix.
Oliver Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Merged hotfix to gate refills and increased TTL floor; scheduled full rollout with canary.
resolution_summary: Applied emergency mitigations (re-enabled warmers, enforced TTL floor, added refill coalescing). Root cause: config encoding mismatch causing per-shard TTL desync and cache-refill stampedes. Permanent fixes merged and scheduled for rollout; follow-up observability and runbook updates planned.

Deploy coalescing gate and warmers improvements (PR #492) with canary in us-east
Add refill-concurrency metric and alert to the SRE dashboard
Update KV cache runbook with mitigation steps and customer notification template
Follow up with LexiChat post-rollout and confirm SLA closure
